title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 64
paragraphs: For this reason the name Demaratus (“prayer of the people”) was given to him. As time went on, Ariston died, and Demaratus obtained the kingdom; but it was fated, apparently, that these things should become known and cause Demaratus to be deposed from his kingdom. That is why Demaratus came to be greatly at variance with Cleomenes, both on that earlier occasion when he withdrew the army from Eleusis, and especially now, when Cleomenes had crossed over to seize those Aeginetans who had gone over to the Medes.
